# GDP Rankings of Top 15 Economies (1970–2025)

## Overview
This dataset tracks the nominal GDP rankings of 15 major economies across six decade-level snapshots: 1970, 1980, 1990, 2000, 2010, and 2025. It is designed for a bump chart showing how country rankings shift over time.

## Data Source

### gdp_rankings
- **country** (string): Name of the country. 15 unique values.
- **1970, 1980, 1990, 2000, 2010, 2025** (integer): Each column represents the country's GDP rank in that year, where 1 = largest nominal GDP. Ranks range from 1 to 15, with no ties within a given year.
- **highlight_countries** (array): Three countries flagged for visual emphasis — China, Japan, and India.
- **unit**: Rank position (1 = highest GDP). Lower number = larger economy.

## Data Notes
- Rankings are approximate and based on nominal GDP in current US dollars at each snapshot year.
- The 2025 figures reflect IMF and World Bank projections and estimates.
- Russia's pre-1991 ranking is an approximation based on the Russian SFSR's estimated share of Soviet GDP.
- Rankings are simplified to 15 slots; some borderline economies (e.g., Netherlands, Indonesia) are excluded for clarity.
- Each year column contains a complete 1–15 permutation with no duplicate ranks.

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import matplotlib.patches as mpatches
import numpy as np

# Data
countries_data = [
    {"country": "United States", "1970": 1, "1980": 1, "1990": 1, "2000": 1, "2010": 1, "2025": 1},
    {"country": "Japan", "1970": 3, "1980": 2, "1990": 2, "2000": 2, "2010": 3, "2025": 4},
    {"country": "Germany", "1970": 2, "1980": 3, "1990": 3, "2000": 3, "2010": 4, "2025": 3},
    {"country": "France", "1970": 4, "1980": 4, "1990": 4, "2000": 5, "2010": 5, "2025": 7},
    {"country": "United Kingdom", "1970": 5, "1980": 5, "1990": 6, "2000": 4, "2010": 6, "2025": 6},
    {"country": "Italy", "1970": 6, "1980": 6, "1990": 5, "2000": 6, "2010": 7, "2025": 9},
    {"country": "Canada", "1970": 7, "1980": 7, "1990": 7, "2000": 7, "2010": 9, "2025": 10},
    {"country": "China", "1970": 9, "1980": 10, "1990": 10, "2000": 6, "2010": 2, "2025": 2},
    {"country": "Brazil", "1970": 8, "1980": 8, "1990": 9, "2000": 9, "2010": 8, "2025": 8},
    {"country": "India", "1970": 13, "1980": 13, "1990": 13, "2000": 12, "2010": 10, "2025": 5},
    {"country": "Australia", "1970": 10, "1980": 11, "1990": 11, "2000": 11, "2010": 13, "2025": 13},
    {"country": "South Korea", "1970": 15, "1980": 15, "1990": 15, "2000": 13, "2010": 14, "2025": 12},
    {"country": "Mexico", "1970": 12, "1980": 12, "1990": 12, "2000": 10, "2010": 11, "2025": 14},
    {"country": "Spain", "1970": 11, "1980": 9, "1990": 8, "2000": 8, "2010": 12, "2025": 15},
    {"country": "Russia", "1970": 14, "1980": 14, "1990": 14, "2000": 14, "2010": 15, "2025": 11},
]

years = [1970, 1980, 1990, 2000, 2010, 2025]
highlight = ["China", "Japan", "India"]

# Colors and styling
highlight_colors = {
    "China": "#D32F2F",    # Bold red
    "Japan": "#1565C0",    # Strong blue
    "India": "#F57F17",    # Rich amber/gold
}

highlight_lw = 4.5
normal_lw = 1.4
normal_color = "#9E9E9E"

# Use a range of muted colors for non-highlight countries to help distinguish them
muted_palette = [
    "#78909C", "#8D6E63", "#7E57C2", "#26A69A", "#5C6BC0",
    "#66BB6A", "#EF5350", "#42A5F5", "#FFA726", "#AB47BC",
    "#8C9EFF", "#FF8A65",
]
muted_idx = 0
country_muted_color = {}
for c in countries_data:
    if c["country"] not in highlight:
        country_muted_color[c["country"]] = muted_palette[muted_idx % len(muted_palette)]
        muted_idx += 1

# Figure setup - editorial style
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(16, 9.5), facecolor="#FAFAF8")
ax.set_facecolor("#FAFAF8")

# Plot non-highlight countries first (background)
for c in countries_data:
    if c["country"] in highlight:
        continue
    ranks = [c[str(y)] for y in years]
    color = country_muted_color[c["country"]]
    ax.plot(years, ranks, color=color, linewidth=normal_lw, alpha=0.55, solid_capstyle="round", zorder=1)
    # End label
    ax.text(2026, ranks[-1], f"  {c['country']}", va="center", ha="left",
            fontsize=8.5, color=color, alpha=0.7, fontweight="medium")

# Plot highlight countries on top
for c in countries_data:
    if c["country"] not in highlight:
        continue
    ranks = [c[str(y)] for y in years]
    color = highlight_colors[c["country"]]
    # Glow effect - wider translucent line behind
    ax.plot(years, ranks, color=color, linewidth=highlight_lw + 5, alpha=0.10, solid_capstyle="round", zorder=2)
    ax.plot(years, ranks, color=color, linewidth=highlight_lw + 2, alpha=0.15, solid_capstyle="round", zorder=2)
    # Main line
    ax.plot(years, ranks, color=color, linewidth=highlight_lw, alpha=0.95, solid_capstyle="round", zorder=3)
    # Data points
    ax.scatter(years, ranks, color=color, s=50, zorder=4, edgecolors="white", linewidths=1.2)
    # End label - bold
    ax.text(2026, ranks[-1], f"  {c['country']}", va="center", ha="left",
            fontsize=11, color=color, fontweight="bold")

# Rank annotations for highlight countries at key positions
# China: show rank 9 at 1970, rank 2 at 2025
ax.annotate("Rank 9", xy=(1970, 9), xytext=(1968.5, 9), fontsize=7.5,
            color=highlight_colors["China"], fontweight="bold", ha="right", va="center", alpha=0.85)
ax.annotate("Rank 2", xy=(2025, 2), xytext=(2024, 2.6), fontsize=7.5,
            color=highlight_colors["China"], fontweight="bold", ha="right", va="top", alpha=0.85)

# Japan: rank 2 in 1990, rank 4 in 2025
ax.annotate("Rank 2", xy=(1990, 2), xytext=(1989, 2.6), fontsize=7.5,
            color=highlight_colors["Japan"], fontweight="bold", ha="right", va="top", alpha=0.85)
ax.annotate("Rank 4", xy=(2025, 4), xytext=(2024, 4.6), fontsize=7.5,
            color=highlight_colors["Japan"], fontweight="bold", ha="right", va="top", alpha=0.85)

# India: rank 13 in 1990, rank 5 in 2025
ax.annotate("Rank 13", xy=(1990, 13), xytext=(1989, 12.4), fontsize=7.5,
            color=highlight_colors["India"], fontweight="bold", ha="right", va="bottom", alpha=0.85)
ax.annotate("Rank 5", xy=(2025, 5), xytext=(2024, 5.6), fontsize=7.5,
            color=highlight_colors["India"], fontweight="bold", ha="right", va="top", alpha=0.85)

# Axes
ax.set_ylim(15.8, 0.2)  # Inverted: rank 1 at top
ax.set_xlim(1968, 2048)

ax.set_xticks(years)
ax.set_xticklabels([str(y) for y in years], fontsize=11, fontweight="medium", color="#424242")

ax.set_yticks(range(1, 16))
ax.set_yticklabels([str(i) for i in range(1, 16)], fontsize=9, color="#757575")

# Grid
ax.grid(axis="x", color="#E0E0E0", linewidth=0.5, linestyle="-", alpha=0.6)
ax.grid(axis="y", color="#EEEEEE", linewidth=0.4, linestyle="--", alpha=0.5)

# Axis labels
ax.set_xlabel("Year", fontsize=12, fontweight="semibold", color="#424242", labelpad=10)
ax.set_ylabel("GDP Rank (1 = Largest Economy)", fontsize=12, fontweight="semibold", color="#424242", labelpad=10)

# Title
ax.set_title("The Rise and Reshuffling of the World's Largest Economies",
             fontsize=20, fontweight="bold", color="#212121", pad=25, loc="left")

# Subtitle
ax.text(0, 1.02, "GDP ranking of top 15 economies, 1970–2025  |  Nominal GDP in current USD",
        transform=ax.transAxes, fontsize=11, color="#757575", ha="left", va="bottom")

# Legend for highlight countries
legend_elements = [
    mpatches.Patch(facecolor=highlight_colors["China"], label="China  (9 → 2)"),
    mpatches.Patch(facecolor=highlight_colors["Japan"], label="Japan  (2 → 4)"),
    mpatches.Patch(facecolor=highlight_colors["India"], label="India  (13 → 5)"),
]
legend = ax.legend(handles=legend_elements, loc="lower left", fontsize=10,
                   frameon=True, framealpha=0.9, edgecolor="#E0E0E0",
                   title="Highlighted Trajectories", title_fontsize=10.5,
                   bbox_to_anchor=(0.0, 0.01))
legend.get_title().set_fontweight("bold")
legend.get_title().set_color("#424242")

# Clean up spines
for spine in ax.spines.values():
    spine.set_color("#BDBDBD")
    spine.set_linewidth(0.5)
ax.spines["top"].set_visible(False)
ax.spines["right"].set_visible(False)

ax.tick_params(axis="both", which="both", length=0)

plt.tight_layout(rect=[0, 0, 1, 0.96])
plt.savefig("/app/output/result.png", dpi=180, bbox_inches="tight",
            facecolor="#FAFAF8", edgecolor="none", pad_inches=0.4)
plt.close()
print("Chart saved successfully.")
